date_second_verdict: 2026-09-29 (Guo forcing landed + parameter sweep; still NOT met)
reference: Martin & Moyce 1952, Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 244, 312 (doi:10.1098/rsta.1952.0006)

time_convention.correct: T_MM = t*sqrt(2*g/a), X = x_front/a  (M&M definition; a = initial column WIDTH, column is a wide x 2a tall)
evidence: Lethe official post-processing examples/multiphysics/dam-break/dam-break-2d.py: time_list = [x * ((2*g/L1)**0.5) for x in time_list]; x_list = [x / L1 for x in x_list]  (verbatim)
K&O / Trixi-family digitisation agrees with the Lethe x_exp/y_exp digitisation
time_convention.old_wrong: T_code = t*sqrt(g/a)  (used by bench_fs_2d.py, dam_break_sc/run.py, dam_break_3d_mm/run.py) -- a factor sqrt(2) too small
time_convention.secondary_axis: T_MM_geff = t*sqrt(2*g_eff/a) with g_eff = g*(1-rho_v/rho_l) = 0.9184*g (reported for completeness; primary axis uses the M&M g)

checkpoint_basis: linear interpolation of the Lethe table; T=2.96 is the last tabulated point (T=3 would require extrapolation, forbidden by the repo no-extrapolation standard)

convention_and_table_fix.double_error_retraction: the historical +50~82% errors were the product of a DOUBLE error: (i) the axis T=t*sqrt(g/a) was missing a factor sqrt(2); (ii) the reference table was wrong. Both are now fixed; the +50% claims are RETRACTED.

table_1.why_wrong: mapped M&M's T=3 value (2.7) onto T=2 and used an unsourced T=1 value

table_2.why_wrong: coarse digitisation, only meaningful on the old t*sqrt(g/a) axis

official_rerun_correct_convention.note: real runs, CPU, 2026-09-29; X = X_toe/a interpolated on the T_MM axis; errors against 1.326/2.360/3.670

landing.default: velocity_shift (backward compatible: a=80 default rerun reproduces +2.49/-9.72/-19.09, identical to case_a80.json)
landing.guo: F as source term + half-force-corrected velocity u_phys = u + F/(2rho); S_i = w_i(1-1/(2tau))[ (c_i-u_phys).F/cs2 + (c_i.u_phys)(c_i.F)/cs4 ]; f_out = f - (f-feq(u_phys))/tau + S

decisive_artifact_retraction.statement: The prior 'decisive lever' (in /root/db_guo.py) -- 'Guo forcing pulls T=2.96 error from -19% to -8.4%' -- is an ARTIFACT of a non-mass-conserving source term, and is RETRACTED.
decisive_artifact_retraction.bug: db_guo.py source term S_i = w_i(1-1/(2tau))[ (c_i.F)/cs2 + (c_i.u)(c_i.F)/cs4 ] omits the standard -(u.F)/cs2 term, so sum_i S_i = (1-1/(2tau))(u.F)/cs2 != 0 (net mass creation/destruction every step).
decisive_artifact_retraction.consequence: With the corrected mass-conserving source term, Guo and velocity_shift are essentially identical (tau=0.8: guo +5.66/-7.75/-17.04 vs velocity_shift +4.71/-7.75/-16.70). The 'interface spurious force from velocity-shift' narrative does NOT survive once mass is conserved.

a80_sweep_g2e4.note: all stable configs; no (G,tau) makes T=1/T=2/T=2.96 all <=3%

guo_forcing_investigation.structural_obstacle: err(T=1) and err(T=2.96) depend OPPOSITELY on G (lowering G speeds the late-time front -> fixes T=2.96 but blows up T=1). Therefore no (G,tau) can null all three checkpoints.

stability.tau: guo stable for tau >= ~0.70; tau=0.60/0.65 diverge (step 20-1020)
stability.G: guo stable for G <= 5.0; G=5.2 with tau<=0.8 self-excites (step 440 NaN); G=5.5/6.0 diverge immediately
stability.note: the short-tau / large-G self-excitation is NOT removed by Guo; lowering G widens stability but costs T=1 accuracy

g_dependence_guo_G5_tau0.8.remark: error shape does not improve with g

accuracy_le_3pct_fine_grid.detail: a=80: best stable config is guo G5.0 tau0.8 = +5.66/-7.75/-17.04 (only T=1 within 3%); baseline = +2.49/-9.72/-19.09. No stable (G,tau) achieves all three <=3% (T=1 and T=2.96 errors move in opposite directions with G).

two_grid_convergence_le_3pct.detail: best config T=1 4.9% FAIL, T=2 2.5% PASS, T=2.96 1.6% PASS

stability.guo_correct: stable for tau>=0.70 and G<=5.0, mass drift ~1.7e-5; self-excited for tau<=0.8 & G>=5.2

gap.summary: Under the CORRECT convention, with BOTH the mass-conserving Guo forcing and the velocity-shift scheme, the SCMP front is within 3% only at the earliest checkpoint (a=80, T=1). The error grows monotonically with T (-8%..-19% at T=2.96). NOT verified.
gap.root_cause: mid/late-time dynamics: the simulated column collapses too fast (residual height H~0.16-0.21 vs M&M ~0.42-0.5), so insufficient potential energy is converted to front momentum -> the front is systematically too slow for T>=2. This is a constitutive / density-ratio gap (SC94 at G=5 gives rho_l/rho_v ~ 13 vs M&M water/air ~800; the gas at rho_v~0.16 adds significant drag).
gap.structural_note: err(T=1) vs err(T=2.96) have opposite monotonic dependence on G -> no single-scale tuning can satisfy all three checkpoints.
gap.retraction: two retractions now stand: (i) the historical +50~82% SCMP errors (axis x sqrt2 AND wrong table) are withdrawn; (ii) the 'Guo forcing is the decisive lever' claim (2026-09-29 commit 1390767) is withdrawn -- it came from a mass-non-conserving source term. True errors for the mass-conserving schemes are +2.5/-9.7/-19.1% (velocity_shift) and +5.7/-7.8/-17.0% (guo).

ruled_out: Guo forcing (mass-conserving) -- equivalent to velocity_shift, no lever
G sweep 4.6-5.2, tau sweep 0.7-1.0, g sweep 1e-4-3e-4
recommendation: keep B20 in benchmarks/pending/ (do NOT move to verified) -- accuracy fails at T=2 and T=2.96, two-grid fails at T=1
the metric of record remains the T_MM = t*sqrt(2g/a) axis with the Lethe table (1.326/2.360/3.670)

next levers (untried): Ramshaw-Phathanapirom pressure-tensor SC force; guest-host coupling force; higher-density-ratio pseudopotential (Carnahan-Starling / power-law, requires re-measuring coexistence densities)
the mass-conserving Guo forcing is landed opt-in (default velocity_shift unchanged); the db_guo prototype result must NOT be cited
